projects.title: PocketBuddy
projects.shortDescription: A web and Android product that captures payments, forecasts allowance runway, coordinates shared purchases, and turns food and travel data into decisions.
projects.fullDescription: I built PocketBuddy end to end across a Kotlin Android connector, FastAPI and MongoDB services, a React interface, and AWS infrastructure. Deterministic code calculates runway and affordability before Amazon Bedrock writes short guidance from those facts. The product covers transaction capture, statement review, shared purchases, food routines, local travel, and privacy controls.
implementation: Built the complete web and mobile product, including the Kotlin connector, FastAPI services, MongoDB data layer, and React interface
Kept runway and affordability calculations deterministic, then constrained Bedrock Nova Lite to explain backend facts without inventing amounts or recommendations
Sent mobile events through API Gateway, Lambda, SQS, a dead-letter queue, and DynamoDB so retries remain traceable and duplicate transactions are rejected
Maintained 166 passing Python tests across payments, statement imports, privacy controls, forecasting, and shared purchases

projects.title: GitLore
projects.shortDescription: A service that turns pull requests, reviews, and repository history into searchable engineering decisions with cited answers and GitHub automation.
projects.fullDescription: Built with a four-person team at HackByte 4.0, GitLore converts GitHub pull-request history into a searchable knowledge graph. Engineers can ask why a decision was made, trace a line from blame to its pull request, and receive answers with source citations. The system spans a React web app, a Chrome extension, GitHub webhooks, and a Hono backend with more than 35 endpoints.
implementation: Mapped pull-request metadata, discussions, reviews, and webhooks into a searchable decision graph exposed through 35+ backend endpoints
Verified GitHub webhook signatures before duplicate-decision checks and kept draft-PR creation behind a user-triggered apply step
Protected routes with API-key and signed-cookie authentication and validated request bodies with Zod
Fell back from Atlas Vector Search to in-memory cosine, text, and regex search when indexes or embeddings were unavailable

projects.title: TinyRF-KD
projects.shortDescription: An edge intrusion-detection study that compresses a large random-forest teacher into KB-scale neural students, then checks explanations and microcontroller behavior.
projects.fullDescription: TinyRF-KD studies whether a strong tabular intrusion-detection teacher can be compressed for constrained hardware without hiding failures in class behavior, explanation agreement, or deployment. The work covers multi-seed evaluation on WSN-DS, SHAP faithfulness, fixed-point C export, and hardware-in-the-loop replay on ESP32-C3 and Arduino R4. The repository is public and the paper is still being written.
implementation: Compressed an 85,064 KB random-forest teacher into 4.64 KB and 13.27 KB neural students with 0.920 and 0.934 macro-F1 across 10 seeds
Measured a 0.047 Spearman correlation between global student and teacher SHAP rankings despite 98.69% and 98.91% student accuracy
Generated fixed-point C models with 1,348-byte and 3,700-byte parameter footprints
Replayed 56,200 test vectors on ESP32-C3 and Arduino R4 with 100% agreement against fixed-point reference outputs

projects.title: Covid-RARS
projects.shortDescription: A reliability study testing whether COVID respiratory-audio models survive participant, temporal, and cross-dataset shifts instead of only performing well in one split.
projects.fullDescription: Covid-RARS examines how respiratory-audio models behave when evaluation becomes stricter. It compares cough, breath, and speech pipelines on participant-disjoint and time-aware Coswara splits, then tests cough-only transfer to COUGHVID. The study also audits metadata shortcuts, feature stability, calibration, and decision utility. The repository is public and the paper is still being written.
implementation: Reached 0.895 AUROC and 0.862 AUPRC with validation-only cough-speech fusion on 314 participant-disjoint holdouts
Evaluated modality-matched transfer across 8,331 external COUGHVID recordings, where source AUROC of 0.849 to 0.868 fell to 0.523 to 0.543
Measured only 0.074 Jaccard overlap between early and late acoustic feature sets
Found a metadata-only model reaching 0.964 AUROC, exposing temporal instability and collection-context shortcuts

projects.title: ArthSaathi
projects.shortDescription: A mutual-fund analysis product that runs deterministic portfolio calculations through nine specialized agents and streams each stage to the interface.
projects.fullDescription: Built for the Economic Times GenAI Hackathon 2026, ArthSaathi turns mutual-fund CAS statements into an explainable portfolio report. Nine specialized agents parse the statement, enrich NAV data, calculate returns and costs, check overlap and benchmarks, project outcomes, score portfolio health, and prepare advice. Financial calculations stay deterministic while language models explain the computed results.
implementation: Orchestrated nine agents for CAS parsing, NAV enrichment, XIRR, overlap, TER, benchmark comparison, projections, portfolio scoring, and recommendations
Ran independent returns and overlap work concurrently with asyncio.gather and streamed start, progress, warning, and completion events through Server-Sent Events
Calculated portfolio metrics in deterministic Python code instead of asking a language model to produce financial values
Routed explanations through Claude, OpenAI, then Gemini, with a rule-based report when no provider returns usable content
